hens_rule_text: up to 6 hens per detached single-family lot (raised from 5 to 6 to match the 2024 state law ARS 9-462.12); no roosters
permit_notes: No coop permit is required unless the coop exceeds 120 sq ft or 7 ft in height, or is connected to electricity or water, in which case a building permit is required regardless of size.
setback_notes: Coop's outer edge must be at least 5 ft from any property line (not stated as a distance from a neighboring home specifically); chickens must stay within the rear and side yards.
coop_rules: Chickens must be housed in a secured coop that does not exceed the height of the surrounding property wall; droppings must be removed from the coop at least twice weekly and from the property at least once a week.
zoning_notes: Rule is citywide under Chandler City Code Sec. 14-33 (Backyard Chickens, Ordinance 5035), first adopted effective Jan. 5, 2023 and updated to raise the cap from 5 to 6 hens for compliance with 2024 state law HB 2325 (A.R.S. 9-462.12).
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: Multiple official City of Chandler pages (the code page itself, a council memo and a news item on the 2024 state-law update) consistently describe Sec. 14-33: originally 5 hens, no roosters, 5 ft coop setback from property lines, coop height and cleaning rules, and the later increase to 6 hens to match state law.
